regions.name: Kartli-Kakheti (eastern Georgia, incl. Borchali, Kazakh-Shamshadil, Lori)
regions.geometry_note: Modern Kakheti, Kvemo Kartli, Tbilisi, Shida Kartli, Mtskheta-Mtianeti, plus the Muslim-ruled marches that were in the Georgian king's orbit in 1800 (Qazakh/Agstafa/Tovuz = Kazakh-Shamshadil sultanates; Armenian Tavush and Lori). Samtskhe-Javakheti (Ottoman Akhaltsikhe pashalik), Imereti, Guria, Samegrelo and Abkhazia are excluded: no Tehran claim found, although Gulistan Art. 3 names them. Frontier zone: borders of the marches are approximate.

regions.name: Shuragel (Shirak plain, Gyumri area)
regions.geometry_note: Modern Shirak province. Shuragel/Shoragol was a Muslim sultanate on the Georgian-Erivan frontier; its exact extent is uncertain.

regions.name: Ganja Khanate
regions.geometry_note: Ganja city and surrounding districts (Goranboy, Goygol, Shamkir, Dashkasan, Gadabay, Samukh, Naftalan). Pre-1880 frontier zone: khanate limits fluid; Qazakh/Shamshadil are in f_kartli_kakheti.

regions.name: Karabakh Khanate (excluding Shusha), incl. Zangezur
regions.geometry_note: Lowland and highland Karabakh plus Zangezur (Syunik); Shusha is a separate region so that the 1826 hold-out can be shown. Frontier zone; khanate edges (esp. Zangezur/Meghri and the Kura lowlands) are approximate.

regions.name: Shusha (fortress and district)
regions.geometry_note: Shusha city + Shusha district: Karabakh's capital, held by a Russian garrison and Armenian defenders through the 1826 Persian siege.

regions.name: Shaki Khanate
regions.geometry_note: Shaki city and district, Qabala and Oghuz. Qakh/Zaqatala/Balakan (Elisu sultanate, Jar-Belokan) are NOT mapped: only nominal Safavid-era overlordship found, no distinct Qajar claim.

regions.name: Shirvan Khanate (incl. Salyan lowlands)
regions.geometry_note: Shamakhi, Agsu, Ismailli, Gobustan and the Kura-Aras lowlands (Hajigabul to Salyan/Neftchala). Khanate had 17 mahals; boundaries with Quba, Baku and Mughan are approximate.

regions.name: Baku Khanate
regions.geometry_note: Baku city, Absheron peninsula and Sumqayit.

regions.name: Quba Khanate
regions.geometry_note: Quba, Qusar, Khachmaz, Khizi, Shabran, Siazan. Quba and Derbent were united under Shaykh Ali Khan 1802-06.

regions.name: Derbent Khanate (Derbent coast, southern Dagestan)
regions.geometry_note: Derbent city and district plus Magaramkent and Suleyman-Stalsky; the khanate was a narrow coastal strip.

regions.name: Southern Dagestan (Tabasaran, Kaytag, Kura, Akhty, Rutul)
regions.geometry_note: Highland districts south of the Shamkhal/Avar lands. Extent of Tehran's nominal claim is poorly defined; Chechnya and northern Dagestan were never claimed.

regions.name: Talysh Khanate, northern part ceded at Gulistan (Lankaran, Astara-north, Masally, Mughan lowlands)
regions.geometry_note: Split of the Talysh khanate: Gulistan gave Russia 'the greater part of Talysh north of the Astara river' and 'the better part of Moghan'; the remainder (Zuvand highlands) went in 1828. Districts allocated to each cession are approximate; the 1813-18 delimitation commission fixed the real line.

regions.name: Talysh Khanate remainder (Zuvand highlands) ceded at Turkmenchay
regions.geometry_note: Lerik and Yardymli (Zuvand). Turkmenchay Art. 4 draws the line 'along the mountain chain separating Zuvand and Arsh'. Which districts were Persian between 1813 and 1828 is approximate.

regions.name: Erivan Khanate (incl. Surmali/Igdir, Sharur-Daralayaz)
regions.geometry_note: Yerevan, Ararat, Armavir, Kotayk and Aragatsotn plains plus Igdir (Surmali) and the Sharur-Sadarak lowlands. Gokcha/Sevan (Gegharkunik) is a separate region; Vayots Dzor is with Nakhchivan; Lori/Shirak with Georgia. Approximate mahal limits.

regions.name: Gokcha / Lake Sevan zone (Gegharkunik)
regions.geometry_note: Modern Gegharkunik. The northern shore was seized by Russia in 1825 on the argument that Gulistan's vague frontier gave it the district.

regions.name: Nakhchivan Khanate (Nakhchivan, Julfa, Vayots Dzor)
regions.geometry_note: Modern Nakhchivan districts except Ordubad (separate) and Sharur/Sadarak (Erivan), plus Vayots Dzor, which Wikipedia attributes to the khanate.

regions.name: Ordubad
regions.geometry_note: Ordubad district, on the Aras; part of the Nakhchivan khanate but occupied separately.

regions.name: Abbasabad bridgehead (right bank of the Aras)

custom.note: semicircle of ~1.5 versts (1.6 km) radius round Abbasabad fortress on the Iranian (right) bank of the Aras; fortress later drowned by the Aras reservoir

regions.geometry_note: Tiny parcel inside modern Iran. Centre taken at the Aras border near the Aras dam/reservoir (~39.07N 45.40E); true fortress position uncertain by several km.

regions.name: Firuzeh (Firyuza oasis and district, Kopet Dag)

custom.note: Firyuza, ~38 km west of Ashgabat in the Kopet Dag

regions.geometry_note: Oasis and adjacent district ceded in 1893. Centre approximate; radius is illustrative (district area not found). NOT the Firuzeh county of Razavi Khorasan.

regions.name: Akhal-Atek oases and Tejen (Turkmen lands under the Kopet Dag)
regions.geometry_note: Gokdepe, Ak Bugday, Baherden, Kaka (Abivard), Babadayhan and Tejen: the Tekke oases whose overlordship Tehran claimed until 1881. The Iranica phrase is 'lands beyond the Tejen... Meyhana, Abivard, Nesa and Marv'.

regions.name: Merv oasis (Mary)
regions.geometry_note: Mary-Bayramaly-Murgap oasis; approximate.

regions.name: Old Sarakhs (Serakhs, north/east bank)
regions.geometry_note: Serakhs district across the Hari Rud from Iranian Sarakhs.

regions.name: Bayezid / Toprakkale district (Ottoman, held by Iran 1821-23)
regions.geometry_note: Dogubayazit (Bayezid), Diyadin, Caldiran, Eleskirt (Toprakkale); the extent of Abbas Mirza's occupation is approximate.

regions.name: Baban emirate / Shahrizor (Sulaymaniyah)
regions.geometry_note: Modern Sulaymaniyah governorate as proxy for the Baban principality (Sulaymaniyah, Shahrizor, Qara Dagh); real extent shifted.

regions.name: Zohab lowlands (west), around Khanaqin
regions.geometry_note: Khanaqin district as proxy for the 'lowlands in the western part of the province of Zohab' ceded in 1847. The 1847 text gives no coordinates; the line was fixed by the 1913-14 commission.

regions.name: Zohab 'Transferred Territory' (1913)

custom.note: rectangle approximating the Persian-held area west of Qasr-e Shirin evacuated in 1914; coordinates are a guess within Khanaqin district

regions.geometry_note: Location and extent are NOT verified: sources say Persia evacuated a 'Transferred Territory' in the Zohab sector under the 1913 Protocol (Anglo-Persian Oil Co. rights safeguarded), the area around Qasr-e Shirin/Naft Khaneh east of the Sirwan; Qasr-e Shirin town stayed Persian.

regions.name: Kotur-neighbourhood strip ceded to Turkey in 1932

custom.note: strip ~6-7 km wide on the Turkish side of the present border west of Qotur; ~90 sq mi (233 km2) per Iranica; position approximate

regions.geometry_note: Iranica: the 1932 line left Turkey 'ninety square miles in the neighbourhood of Kotur' (between Guirberan and Kuch Dagh). Exact location not verified.

regions.name: Little Ararat zone ceded to Turkey in 1932

custom.note: ~60 sq mi (155 km2) strip west of the present Iran-Turkey border east of Little Ararat; position approximate

regions.geometry_note: A British diplomat's cable put the northern zone at about 60 square miles, giving Turkey control of all Lesser Ararat; exact line not verified.

regions.name: Muhammarah (Khorramshahr) and Khizr island (Abadan)
regions.geometry_note: Inside modern Iran. Included only because its sovereignty was disputed with the Ottomans before 1847; the internal agent may overlay the Ka'b/Muhaisin sheikhdom (indirect) for 1812-1925.

regions.name: Shatt al-Arab (Arvand Rud), eastern half-channel, Khaiin canal to the sea

custom.note: schematic strip along the Iranian side of the 1975 thalweg line (points from IBS 164: Nahr Khaiin junction 30.448N 48.106E to the mouth 29.853N 48.745E); real half-channel is only ~0.3-0.8 km wide, so render as a stroked line

regions.geometry_note: The river is an international boundary river; the thalweg (median line of the main navigable channel) was agreed in 1975. Strip is schematic.

regions.name: Muhammarah anchorage reach (Khaiin canal to the Karun mouth)

custom.note: short reach round the Karun/Shatt junction; Persian jurisdiction recognised in 1847 and 1913

regions.geometry_note: 'The modern port and anchorage of Muhammara, above and below the junction of the river Karun with the Shatt al-Arab' (1913 Protocol); extent of the reach is approximate.

regions.name: Shatt al-Arab opposite Abadan (thalweg segment of 1937)

custom.note: ~4 miles from the end of Choteit island (30.29N 48.32E) to opposite Jetty No. 1 at Abadan (30.336N 48.270E)

regions.geometry_note: Segment where the 1937 treaty moved the boundary from the Iranian low-water mark to the thalweg.

regions.name: Al-Faw peninsula
regions.geometry_note: Al-Faw district.

regions.name: Majnoon Islands (Hawizeh marshes)
regions.geometry_note: Operation Kheibar captured ~160 km2 with ~50 oil wells.

regions.name: Haj Omran highlands (Iraqi Kurdistan)
regions.geometry_note: Operation Dawn 2 seized ~390 km2.

regions.name: Penjwin valley (Iraqi Kurdistan)

custom.note: ~466 km2 captured in Operation Dawn 4, centred on Penjwin

regions.geometry_note: Penjwin valley and villages.

regions.name: Halabja district (Iraqi Kurdistan)
regions.geometry_note: Halabcha district; Operation Dawn 10 also took Dojileh and Khurmal.

regions.name: Herat and Farah (Herat principality)
regions.geometry_note: Modern Herat and Farah provinces as the Sadozai principality and its dependencies (Ghurian, Sabzawar/Shindand, Lash-Juwayn). Ghurian was not split out: no reliable separate chronology found.

regions.name: Kandahar (Barakzai principality)
regions.geometry_note: Kandahar province.

regions.name: Afghan Sistan (Nimruz: Chakhansur, Kang, Zaranj)
regions.geometry_note: Modern Nimruz province (Goldsmid's 'Outer Seistan', the right/east bank of the Helmand and lands beyond).

regions.name: Kech and Panjgur (Makran)
regions.geometry_note: Modern Kech and Panjgur districts: the Gichki/Kalat lands assigned to Kalat by the 1871 Goldsmid line (Panjgur, Parum, Buleda, Mand, Tump, Kech, Dasht). Gwadar (Omani) not mapped.

regions.name: Kuhak district

custom.note: Kuhak village 27.132N 63.240E; Iran's easternmost point area

regions.geometry_note: Small district awarded to Kalat in 1871, reclaimed by Iran, occupied May 1874, formally Iranian in 1896. Radius illustrative.

regions.name: Mirjaveh frontier parcel

custom.note: Mirjaveh town 29.015N 61.450E; the disputed strip along the Mirjawa river/Kila Safaid

regions.geometry_note: Disputed 1896-1905 between the Holdich line's 'blue' reading and Persian possession; radius illustrative.

regions.name: Chabahar (Omani appanage)
regions.geometry_note: Inside modern Iran; included because it was a Muscat/Omani possession.

regions.name: Bahrain
regions.geometry_note: Archipelago (four governorates).

regions.name: Abu Musa
regions.geometry_note: Island at 25.87N 55.03E.

regions.name: Greater Tunb
regions.geometry_note: Island at 26.264N 55.307E.

regions.name: Lesser Tunb
regions.geometry_note: Island at 26.244N 55.147E.

regions.name: Sirri island
regions.geometry_note: Inside modern Iran; parcel because the Qasimi deputy-governors of Lengeh held it.

events.title: Treaty of Gulistan
events.summary: Signed 12 Oct OS (24 Oct NS; Iranica: 29 Shawwal 1228) at Gulistan; ratified at Tbilisi Sept 1814. sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 164 (1978), Iran-Iraq Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs164.pdf)

events.title: Iran-Iraq frontier treaty (Tehran)
events.summary: Reaffirmed the 1913 Protocol and 1914 minutes except off Abadan, where the boundary moved to the thalweg (Choteit island to Jetty No. 1).
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 164 (1978), Iran-Iraq Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs164.pdf)

events.title: Iran abrogates the 1937 treaty
events.summary: Iran repudiated the 1937 treaty, stopped paying Iraq dues and escorted ships down the river (Joint Operation Arvand, 22-25 Apr 1969), claiming the thalweg as the frontier.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 164 (1978), Iran-Iraq Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs164.pdf)
Wikipedia, 'Shatt al-Arab dispute' and 'Joint Operation Arvand' (cross-check only)

events.title: Algiers Accord (joint communique)
events.summary: Shah and Saddam Hussein agreed to demarcate the land border on the 1913 Protocol and 1914 minutes and the river border on the thalweg; Iran ended support for Iraqi Kurds. Tehran protocol 15-17 March 1975.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 164 (1978), Iran-Iraq Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs164.pdf)

events.title: Baghdad treaty on the State Boundary
events.summary: Treaty plus three protocols: land boundary redemarcation, river boundary on the thalweg (105 km), border security. Zain al-Qaws and Saif Saad were to pass to Iraq but were never handed over; their location was not verified, so they are not mapped as Iranian-held.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 164 (1978), Iran-Iraq Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs164.pdf)
Wikipedia, 'Iraqi invasion of Iran' (cross-check only)

events.title: Iraq abrogates the Algiers Accord
events.summary: Iraq retook Zain al-Qaws and Saif Saad on 10 Sept 1980, Iran declared the accord void 14 Sept and Saddam abrogated it on 17 Sept, five days before the invasion. Tehran maintains the thalweg claim.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 164 (1978), Iran-Iraq Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs164.pdf)
Wikipedia, 'Shatt al-Arab dispute' and 'Iraqi invasion of Iran' (cross-check only)

events.title: Saddam Hussein accepts the 1975 accord
events.summary: Mid-Aug 1990 Iraq restored the 1975 border and thalweg and promised to leave occupied Iranian land (about 2,600 sq km, inside modern Iran).
sources: Christian Science Monitor, 'Iran Jubilant Over Iraq's Proposal but Won't Alter Policy', 17 Aug 1990 (csmonitor.com/1990/0817/oshatt.html)

events.title: Ottoman governor sacks Muhammarah
events.summary: Ali Rida Pasha of Baghdad sacked Muhammarah (Khorramshahr) in 1837, part of the Perso-Ottoman crisis of 1837-43 that led to the Erzurum conference.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Mohammad Shah Qajar' and 'Emirate of Muhammara' (cross-check only)

events.title: Operation Dawn 2: Iran seizes Haj Omran
events.summary: Iranian forces advanced from Piranshahr and took the Haj Omran highlands (~390 km2) in Iraqi Kurdistan.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)
Human Rights Watch, Genocide in Iraq: The Anfal Campaign Against the Kurds (1993), ch. 1

events.title: Operation Dawn 4: Penjwin valley
events.summary: Iran and PUK peshmerga took the Penjwin valley (466 km2); operation ended around 21 Nov 1983.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)
Human Rights Watch, Genocide in Iraq: The Anfal Campaign Against the Kurds (1993), ch. 1

events.title: Operation Kheibar: Majnoon Islands
events.summary: Iranian assault through the Hawizeh marsh took the Majnoon Islands (~160 km2, ~50 oil wells), held until 1988.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)

events.title: Operation Dawn 8: Iran takes Al-Faw
events.summary: Surprise crossing of the Shatt al-Arab (night of 9-10 Feb) captured the Faw peninsula; first major Iranian occupation of Iraqi land.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)

events.title: Operation Karbala-5 (Basra front)
events.summary: Iran seized a sliver of Basra governorate near Duaiji/Fish Lake and held positions around Shalamcheh until Iraq's May 1988 counterattack. Too small to map reliably.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)

events.title: Operation Dawn 10: Halabja captured
events.summary: Iranian forces and peshmerga captured Halabja, Dojileh and Khurmal (14-19 March); Iraqi chemical attack 16-17 March.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)
Christian Science Monitor, 'Iraq adds to string of victories. Iran's faltering forces', 13 July 1988 (csmonitor.com/1988/0713/ohala.html)

events.title: Iraq retakes Al-Faw
events.summary: Operation Ramadan Mubarak (17-18 April 1988) expelled Iranian forces from the peninsula within 35 hours.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)

events.title: Battle of Fish Lake / Shalamcheh
events.summary: Tawakalna 1 pushed Iranian forces out of positions held in Basra governorate since Jan 1987.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)

events.title: Iraq retakes Majnoon
events.summary: Iraqi forces recovered the Majnoon oilfield, 4.5 years after Iran took it.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)
Christian Science Monitor, 'Iranian morale sinks in the marshes', 1 July 1988 (csmonitor.com/1988/0701/omaj.html)

events.title: Iran abandons Halabja
events.summary: Iranian forces left Halabja without a fight, the last major foothold in Iraq.
sources: Christian Science Monitor, 'Iraq adds to string of victories. Iran's faltering forces', 13 July 1988 (csmonitor.com/1988/0713/ohala.html)

events.title: UN-supervised ceasefire
events.summary: Khomeini accepted UNSC Res. 598 in mid-July 1988 (18-20 July); the ceasefire took effect 20 Aug 1988. Iraq's counter-invasion of Iran (about 9,600 km2) ended soon after; no Iraqi territory remained mapped as Iranian-held.
sources: Wikipedia articles on Iran-Iraq War operations (Dawn 2, Dawn-4, Kheibar, Dawn 8, Dawn 10, Karbala-5, Tawakalna ala Allah Operations) (cross-check only)
Wikipedia, 'United Nations Security Council Resolution 598' (cross-check only)

events.title: Persian expedition to Herat (Shahdih)
events.summary: Fath-Ali Shah's forces defeated Firuz al-Din Mirza (battle of Shahdih, 1807); tribute exacted and Persian suzerainty (claimed since c.1801) reasserted, repeated 1814.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Herat vi. The Herat Question' (iranicaonline.org/articles/herat-vi/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

events.title: Barakzai coup in Herat
events.summary: Fath Khan Barakzai deposed Firuz al-Din (April 1818); the Sadozai Mahmud and Kamran then ruled Herat independently of Tehran.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Herat (1793-1863)' (cross-check only)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Herat vi. The Herat Question' (iranicaonline.org/articles/herat-vi/)

events.title: Abbas Mirza's Herat campaign ends
events.summary: Abbas Mirza's army besieged Herat in 1832-33; he died Oct 1833 and his son withdrew after a late-Nov 1833 arrangement with Kamran (hostage, coin and khutba in the shah's name, tribute), per Wikipedia.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Siege of Herat (1833)' (cross-check only)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Herat vi. The Herat Question' (iranicaonline.org/articles/herat-vi/)

events.title: Treaty between Mohammad Shah and the Kandahar sardars
events.summary: The Kandahar sardars (Kohandil Khan) accepted Persian suzerainty during the Herat campaign; Russian diplomacy encouraged the Tehran-Kandahar-Kabul entente. Date and terms not found in detail.
sources: Wikipedia, 'First Herat War' (cross-check only)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Herat vi. The Herat Question' (iranicaonline.org/articles/herat-vi/)

events.title: Siege of Herat (Mohammad Shah)
events.summary: Siege from 23/24 Nov 1837, lasting nearly ten months; the shah withdrew empty-handed on 9 Sept 1838 under British pressure (Kharg occupied).
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Herat vi. The Herat Question' (iranicaonline.org/articles/herat-vi/)
Wikipedia, 'First Herat War' (cross-check only)

events.title: Persian siege of Herat lifted
events.summary: Mohammad Shah lifted the siege on 9 Sept 1838 after the British occupation of Kharg and McNeill's ultimatum.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Herat vi. The Herat Question' (iranicaonline.org/articles/herat-vi/)

events.title: British occupy Kandahar
events.summary: The Army of the Indus entered Kandahar (25 April 1839), ending the Barakzai principality's independence.
sources: Wikipedia, 'First Anglo-Afghan War' (cross-check only)

events.title: Persia relinquishes claims on Kandahar
events.summary: A treaty with the Kandahar chief is reported (India Office Military Report on Persia) to have ended Persian claims to Afghan territory; low confidence, no text seen.
sources: India Office/General Staff, 'Military Report on Persia' (Qatar Digital Library, qdl.qa/en/archive/81055/vdc_100066221357.0x00001d)

events.title: Persian army takes Herat
events.summary: Hesam o-Saltaneh's army, with French engineers, captured Herat (11 or 25 Oct 1856; ceremonial entry 30 Oct). Britain declared war 1 Nov 1856 and landed at Bushehr.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Herat vi. The Herat Question' (iranicaonline.org/articles/herat-vi/)
Wikipedia, 'Second Herat War' (cross-check only)

events.title: Treaty of Paris (Anglo-Persian)
events.summary: Signed 4 March 1857 (ratified 2 May at Baghdad). Art. V: evacuate Herat within three months; Art. VI: Persia relinquishes all claims to Herat and Afghanistan and any tribute, coin or khutba, and accepts British good offices in disputes.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Herat vi. The Herat Question' (iranicaonline.org/articles/herat-vi/)
US Dept of State, Office of the Geographer, International Boundary Study No. 6 (1961), Afghanistan-Iran Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/Digital-Collections/LimitsinSeas/pdf/ibs006.pdf)

events.title: Persian troops leave Herat
events.summary: Persian garrison evacuated by about Sept 1857 after installing Sultan Ahmad Khan in April; Dost Mohammad took Herat 27 May 1863.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Herat (1793-1863)' (cross-check only)

events.title: Persian takeover of western Sistan
events.summary: Persian invasion of Sistan in 1865 with a governor (Hesmat-al-Molk); Persia had been reclaiming Sistan since 1772. Western (modern-Iranian) Sistan is left to the internal agent.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Sistan ii. In the Islamic period' (iranicaonline.org/articles/sistan-ii-islamic-period/)

events.title: Goldsmid's Sistan arbitration
events.summary: Award (1872) split Sistan along the Helmand, giving Persia 'Seistan proper' and Afghanistan the right bank; accepted by both governments in spring 1873. McMahon's 1903-05 award re-fixed it after the river shifted; Persia's shah protested but the award was accepted.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Helmand River iv. In the late 19th and 20th centuries' (iranicaonline.org/articles/helmand-river-iv/)
US Dept of State, Office of the Geographer, International Boundary Study No. 6 (1961), Afghanistan-Iran Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/Digital-Collections/LimitsinSeas/pdf/ibs006.pdf)

events.title: MacLean arbitration (Hashtadan)
events.summary: Hashtadan plain dispute began Mar 1885 when Persians began to cultivate it; MacLean (1888-91) fixed a compromise line from the Hari Rud south to pillar 39 (c. 34 deg 20'N, 60 deg 55'E) with a deflection round Hashtadan mound. Not mapped as a region (extent not found).
sources: US Dept of State, Office of the Geographer, International Boundary Study No. 6 (1961), Afghanistan-Iran Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/Digital-Collections/LimitsinSeas/pdf/ibs006.pdf)

events.title: McMahon Sistan arbitration
events.summary: McMahon's award (Nov 1903) fixed the Helmand/Nad Ali line; 90 pillars placed by 15 May 1905. Accepted by Afghanistan; Mozaffar al-Din Shah protested from Europe but the line stands.
sources: US Dept of State, Office of the Geographer, International Boundary Study No. 6 (1961), Afghanistan-Iran Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/Digital-Collections/LimitsinSeas/pdf/ibs006.pdf)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Helmand River iv. In the late 19th and 20th centuries' (iranicaonline.org/articles/helmand-river-iv/)

events.title: Altay award (Hashtadan plains, Musa Abad)
events.summary: Turkish General Fahreddin Altay delimited the 250-mile central segment (pillars 40-87, passing Musaabad, Yezdan, Kuh-i-Siah) and the Hari Rud north end. Parcels moved are not mapped (areas not found).
sources: US Dept of State, Office of the Geographer, International Boundary Study No. 6 (1961), Afghanistan-Iran Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/Digital-Collections/LimitsinSeas/pdf/ibs006.pdf)

events.title: Tehran claims all Makran and Baluchistan
events.summary: In 1281 AH (1864) Iran officially claimed all Makran and Baluchistan, grounding it in Nader Shah's 1736 conquest.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Cah-bahar' (iranicaonline.org/articles/cah-bahar-...)

events.title: Goldsmid's Perso-Kalat line
events.summary: Notes exchanged 1 and 4 Sept 1871 (Alison for Kalat; Mirza Saeed Khan) fixed the line from Kuhak to Gwatar Bay, leaving Panjgur, Kohuk, Buleda, Mand/Tump/Kech and Dasht with Kalat; Britain kept treating Gwadar as Omani.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 167 (1979), Iran-Pakistan Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs167.pdf)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Cah-bahar' (iranicaonline.org/articles/cah-bahar-...)

events.title: Persia occupies Chabahar
events.summary: Persian forces under Ebrahim Khan took Chabahar from Omani control (21 Feb 1872, 12 Dhu'l-hejja); Iranian since.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Cah-bahar' (iranicaonline.org/articles/cah-bahar-...)

events.title: Iran occupies Kuhak
events.summary: Iran occupied Kuhak in May 1874 after claiming it despite the 1871 line.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 167 (1979), Iran-Pakistan Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs167.pdf)

events.title: Holdich line (Kuhak to Malik Siah)
events.summary: Agreement of 27 Dec 1895, proces-verbal of 24 March 1896 and demarcation agreement of 26 March 1896 formally included Kuhak in Iran; 11 pillars to Gorani. Boundary beyond pillar 11 left open.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 167 (1979), Iran-Pakistan Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs167.pdf)
Wikipedia, 'Thomas Holdich' (cross-check only)

events.title: Anglo-Iranian agreement on Mirjaveh
events.summary: The UK withdrew its claim to Mirjaveh; Iran allowed the British post at Padaha to take water.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 167 (1979), Iran-Pakistan Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs167.pdf)

events.title: Iran-Pakistan boundary agreement
events.summary: Signed at Tehran; confirms the 1871, 1895 and 1896 lines with new sections from Gwatar Bay to Kuhak and from pillar 11 to Malik Siah; demarcated Feb-May 1958 and Oct 1958-Feb 1959; final protocol 8 Dec 1959. No territory changed hands.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 167 (1979), Iran-Pakistan Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs167.pdf)

events.title: Qajar expeditions to Sarakhs, Khwarazm and the Turkmen
events.summary: Abbas Mirza led an expedition to Sarakhs and Khwarazm in 1832, and Mohammad Shah another in 1837 (Iranica: Persia asserted claims to Marv, Khiva and Sarakhs). Khiva/Khwarazm was claimed rhetorically but no sustained claim or administration is documented, so it is not mapped.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Central Asia viii. Relations with Persia in the 19th Century' (iranicaonline.org/articles/central-asia-viii/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

events.title: Disastrous Persian Merv expedition
events.summary: The 1860-61 campaign against Merv (Hesam al-Saltaneh) ended in a crushing defeat, 'the beginning of the end of Iran's claims to dominion over the Khavaran plain'.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Central Asia viii. Relations with Persia in the 19th Century' (iranicaonline.org/articles/central-asia-viii/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

events.title: Russo-Persian agreement on the Atrek
events.summary: Russia recognised the Atrek as the boundary (about 30 miles east of the Caspian); Persia dropped claims north of it.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 25 (rev. 1978), Iran-U.S.S.R. Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs025.pdf)

events.title: Russians storm Geok Tepe
events.summary: Fall of the Tekke fortress (12 Jan 1881 OS) ended Akhal independence.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Battle of Geok Tepe' (cross-check only)
US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 25 (rev. 1978), Iran-U.S.S.R. Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs025.pdf)

events.title: Akhal-Khorasan Convention
events.summary: Convention of 9/21 Dec 1881 (Wikipedia gives 21 Sept) set the frontier east of the Caspian to Babadurmaz and ended Iran's claims beyond the Tejen (Marv, Abivard, Nesa, Meyhana); Firyuza left to Persia.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 25 (rev. 1978), Iran-U.S.S.R. Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs025.pdf)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

events.title: Russia expels Persian garrison from Old Sarakhs
events.summary: Komarov's Russians annexed Merv in 1884 and took Old Sarakhs on the Hari Rud in 1884-85; Persia's claim there ended with the 1893 convention.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Sarakhs' and 'Treaty of Akhal' (cross-check only)

events.title: Convention for territorial interchange (Tehran)
events.summary: Signed 27 May OS (8 June NS) 1893: Persia ceded the Firyuza oasis and district; Russia gave up the Abbasabad bridgehead and the Hissar oasis near Lotfabad, and the frontier east of Babadurmaz to Afghanistan was delimited. Hissar is not mapped (location not verified).
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 25 (rev. 1978), Iran-U.S.S.R. Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs025.pdf)

events.title: Treaty of Friendship (Moscow)
events.summary: Art. III provided for return of Firyuza to Persia and Soviet recognition of Persia's islands off the Astrabad coast; Firyuza was never returned.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 25 (rev. 1978), Iran-U.S.S.R. Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs025.pdf)

events.title: Iran-USSR frontier and financial agreement
events.summary: Signed at Tehran (in force 20 May 1955). Changes in Iran's favour at the Moghan steppe, Dyman, Yedi Evlar island at the Astara mouth, Sarakhs (about 10 sq mi west of the Hari Rud) and a compromise Atrek delta line; Namin adjusted to Soviet gain; Soviet possession of Firyuza confirmed, ending Iran's claim. Parcels other than Firuzeh not mapped (areas small, coordinates not found). Further 1957 demarcation and 1970 Aras reservoir protocol.
sources: US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 25 (rev. 1978), Iran-U.S.S.R. Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs025.pdf)

events.title: Bruce-Farmanfarma agreement on Bahrain
events.summary: Resident William Bruce and Fars governor Hosein Ali Mirza Farmanfarma agreed that Bahrain was 'always subordinate to the province of Fars'; London disowned it, Tehran cited it for a century.
sources: Qatar Digital Library (India Office Records), file 'Persian pretentions to Bahrain' (qdl.qa/en/archive/81055/vdc_100023043274.0x000070)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Bahrain iii. History of political relations with Iran' (iranicaonline.org/articles/bahrain-all/bahrain-iii-history-of-political-relations-with-iran/)

events.title: Persian protest to Britain and the League over Bahrain
events.summary: Persian note protested the Anglo-Saudi Treaty of Jeddah (20 May 1927) and insisted Bahrain was incontestably Persian; copied to the League of Nations.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Bahrain iii. History of political relations with Iran' (iranicaonline.org/articles/bahrain-all/bahrain-iii-history-of-political-relations-with-iran/)

events.title: Majlis declares Bahrain the 14th province
events.summary: Iran formally designated Bahrain its fourteenth province (law of 11-12 Nov 1957).
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Bahrain iii. History of political relations with Iran' (iranicaonline.org/articles/bahrain-all/bahrain-iii-history-of-political-relations-with-iran/)
Wikipedia, 'Bahrain-Iran relations' and 'United Nations Security Council Resolution 278' (cross-check only)

events.title: UN good-offices mission to Bahrain
events.summary: Guicciardi mission 29 March-18 April 1970; report circulated 30 April found Bahrainis virtually unanimous for full independence; Security Council Res. 278 endorsed it on 11 May.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bahrain-Iran relations' and 'United Nations Security Council Resolution 278' (cross-check only)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Bahrain iii. History of political relations with Iran' (iranicaonline.org/articles/bahrain-all/bahrain-iii-history-of-political-relations-with-iran/)

events.title: Iran renounces its claim to Bahrain
events.summary: The Majlis approved the UN report 184-4 on 14 May 1970, the Senate unanimously on 18 May; Bahrain became independent 15 Aug 1971. Tehran date chosen: Majlis vote.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Bahrain iii. History of political relations with Iran' (iranicaonline.org/articles/bahrain-all/bahrain-iii-history-of-political-relations-with-iran/)
Wikipedia, 'Bahrain-Iran relations' and 'United Nations Security Council Resolution 278' (cross-check only)

events.title: Persia takes Sirri and ends the Qasimi deputy-governorship of Lengeh
events.summary: Persia dissolved the Qasimi deputy-governorship at Lengeh and planted its flag on Sirri in 1887; Britain tacitly acquiesced in Aug 1888.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Abu Musa iii. In International Relations' (iranicaonline.org/articles/abu-musa/abu-musa-bu-musa/)

events.title: First documented Persian claim to Abu Musa
events.summary: A Persian military report of 1888 for the British prime minister claimed Abu Musa; Britain neither countered nor objected.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Abu Musa iii. In International Relations' (iranicaonline.org/articles/abu-musa/abu-musa-bu-musa/)

events.title: Competing flag-raising on the Tunbs and Abu Musa
events.summary: Persian and Qasimi flag-hoisting incidents in 1903-04 (a Belgian customs official in Persian service reportedly raised the Persian flag in April 1904; Iranica gives few details); the Tunbs were then administered by Sharjah (1904-21) and Ras al-Khaimah (1921-71).
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Tonb Islands' (iranicaonline.org/articles/tonb/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Abu Musa iii. In International Relations' (iranicaonline.org/articles/abu-musa/abu-musa-bu-musa/)

events.title: Iran-Sharjah memorandum on Abu Musa
events.summary: MoU on shared administration of Abu Musa (Iranian troops in the northern sector, Sharjah police elsewhere); Iranian forces landed on 30 Nov.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Abu Musa iii. In International Relations' (iranicaonline.org/articles/abu-musa/abu-musa-bu-musa/)
Wikipedia, 'Seizure of Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs' (cross-check only)

events.title: Iran seizes the Tunbs
events.summary: After the British withdrawal Iranian forces landed on Greater and Lesser Tunb (30 Nov 1971; some sources say the evening of 29 Nov). There was an armed clash on Greater Tunb (Wikipedia: four Ras al-Khaimah policemen and three Iranian soldiers killed) and the inhabitants were deported to Ras al-Khaimah.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Tonb Islands' (iranicaonline.org/articles/tonb/)
Wikipedia, 'Seizure of Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs' (cross-check only)

events.title: Iran asserts full control of Abu Musa
events.summary: After expelling foreign workers in April 1992 Iran barred Sharjah's teachers on 24 Aug 1992; the UAE says this breaches the 1971 MoU.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Abu Musa iii. In International Relations' (iranicaonline.org/articles/abu-musa/abu-musa-bu-musa/)
Gulf News, 'August 24, 1992: Iran denies UAE teachers entry into Abu Mousa' (gulfnews.com)

events.title: Caspian sector (note only)
events.summary: Tehran's long-held position was equal division of the Caspian (20 per cent each) while Soviet-Iranian treaties (1921, 1940) left no sectoral line; the 2018 Aktau Convention did not fix sectors. Not mapped.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Legal status of the Caspian Sea' (cross-check only)
US Dept of State, International Boundary Study No. 25 (rev. 1978), Iran-U.S.S.R. Boundary (library.law.fsu.edu/.../ibs025.pdf)
